newsitem.title: UK: Partial declaration in zinc options, others dull.
newsitem.headline: Partial declaration in zinc options, others dull.

text.p: A partial declaration in LME zinc call options on Tuesday was followed by a modest surge in futures prices, but the other metals were dull, traders said.
At the declaration, August zinc futures settled just under the $1,600 level, but some of the call options were declared anyway, a trader said.
"I thought that was a bit ambitious, but after they were declared, the back came out and the futures moved higher," he added.
The cash/threes backwardation flared about $20 to $100 and three months ended the morning kerb $14 stronger at $1,512 per tonne.
Open interest in calls at $1,600 was only 85 lots (equivalent to 2,125 tonnes) and at $1,575 was 120 lots (3,000 tonnes), according to LME data at Monday's close.
In aluminium and the other metals, the declaration was uninspiring as futures prices strayed little from previous levels, traders said.
"Absolutely nothing happened at all," one said.
August aluminium futures were holding comfortably above the $1,700 strike, where a good lump of open interest was found -- 1,575 lots (39,375 tonnes).
August was straddling $1,725, where open interest amounted to only 450 lots (11,250 tonnes), where calls were abandoned.
The largest open interest in aluminium -- at $1,650 with 2,252 lots (56,300 tonnes) -- was well in the money.
Very few puts were seen at those levels.
In copper, August futures were at $2,320 at the declaration, so $2,300 calls (1,259 lots or 31,475 tonnes) and $2,350 puts (660 lots or 16,500 tonnes) were declared.
"The only thing that was a remote worry was on copper at the $2,300 strike if prices had come off another $30," one dealer said.
The market failed to come close to the biggest areas of open interest at the $2,400 strike in calls and the $2,000 strike in puts.
Lead settled slightly under $600, well below the lowest strike at $625, where there were 278 lots (6,950 tonnes) of puts.
Activity so far this week in options has been rather thin, with some interest in upside lead calls on Tuesday after futures dived to 22-month lows on Monday, one trader said.
Residual buying has also been seen in aluminium upside calls after last week's sizeable trades in fourth quarter 1997 and first half 1998 material.
On Tuesday morning, business was seen in $1,700 and $1,800 calls for the fourth quarter 1997, LME data showed.
Volatilities in aluminium were firm despite grantors taking advantage of the steady levels to sell more options, traders said.
Aluminium volatilities were expected to remain strong as long as fund buying continued. September at-the-money implied volatility was quoted around 25.0/27.0 percent.

Nearby zinc volatility dipped slightly, as expected, as the underlying market settled following its violent plunge last week. September implied volatility was down two to three points at 38.0/43.0 percent.
